legend: The students at Rubgers University are organizing a programming contest. Since a lot of strong teams will participate, they expect some of them to solve all problems. To distinguish between them, a special prize will be awarded to the team with a special solve order.
The contest consists of N≤26%%ZSMJ0%% problems labelled A%%ZSMJ1%%, B%%ZSMJ2%%, etc: the first N%%ZSMJ3%% letters of the English alphabet.

A solve order for a team is a sequence of letters denoting the order in which it solved all the problems: e.g., for N=3%%ZSMJ4%%, a possible solve order is BAC%%ZSMJ5%% — B%%ZSMJ6%% solved first, then A%%ZSMJ7%%, then C%%ZSMJ8%%. We only consider teams which solve every problem exactly once, so, e.g., AC%%ZSMJ9%% or ABAC%%ZSMJ10%% are not valid solve orders.

Solve order a%%ZSMJ11%% is lexicographically smaller than solve order b%%ZSMJ12%% if, at the first position where they differ, the character in a%%ZSMJ13%% comes in the alphabet before the character in b%%ZSMJ14%%. E.g., ACB%%ZSMJ15%% is lexicographically smaller than BAC%%ZSMJ16%%, which is lexicographically smaller than BCA%%ZSMJ17%%.

Consider all possible solve orders of the N%%ZSMJ18%% problems. Let their number be M%%ZSMJ19%%. Sort the M%%ZSMJ20%% solve orders from lexicographically smallest to largest. In this list, the median solve order is located at position ⌈M2⌉%%ZSMJ21%% (M2%%ZSMJ22%% rounded up).
Any team with the median solve order will get a special prize. Help Rubgers students decide what the order is!
input: The problem consists of T%%ZSMJ23%% independent test cases.
The first line contains a single integer T%%ZSMJ24%% (1≤T≤26%%ZSMJ25%%) — the number of independent test cases to process.
Each of the next T%%ZSMJ26%% lines contains a single integer N%%ZSMJ27%% (1≤N≤26%%ZSMJ28%%) — the number of problems in the contest.
output: For each test case, output a single line containing the median solve order for the contest with N%%ZSMJ29%% problems.
note: In the first test case, N=1%%ZSMJ30%%, so the only solve order is A%%ZSMJ31%%.
In the second test case, the solve orders in lexicographical order are AB,BA%%ZSMJ32%%. The median is AB%%ZSMJ33%%.
In the third test case, the solve orders in lexicographical order are ABC,ACB,BAC,BCA,CAB,CBA%%ZSMJ34%%. The median is BAC%%ZSMJ35%%.
